properties.name: The 53 find_tools misses are two causes, measured apart: 12 have ZERO overlap between the user's words and the tool's text (no ranking can find them), and 41 are crowded out by a scorer that substring-matches, weights stopwords, and never normalises for length — ablation recovers only 17 of 53
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-11 against the 180-query criterion-1 corpus (`fact:find-tools-baseline-53-of-180-tools-are-not-in-the-top-five-for-a-query-in-a-users-words`). This decision stated the mismatch — a problem in the user's words against a tool named for its operation — and offered five options without a measurement of how much of the failure is WHICH kind. Now measured, and it is two kinds, and they want different fixes.

═══ ① A VOCABULARY GAP, 12 of 53 — no ranking change can find these ═══
For twelve missed tools, NOT ONE content word of the user's query appears anywhere in the tool's name, description or parameter names. `add_requirement` ← "write down something the system must do". `graph_report` ← "give me the overall health summary of the design". `get_node` ← "show me everything recorded about this one item". `propose_heal` ← "suggest repairs for the structural problems in the design". `budget_report` ← "which of my declared limits is being exceeded". The surface simply does not contain the user's register for these. Only carrying that register ON THE TOOL — this decision's option (b), a question-shaped phrasing in the description — can reach them, and the corpus is then the check that it was carried.

═══ ② A SCORER THAT CROWDS, 41 of 53 — a class defect in one function ═══
The other 41 have some overlap (median 25% of query words) and lose to tools that merely CONTAIN more words. The mechanism, read from the code and confirmed by measurement: `record_finding` appears in 27 other tools' top-5, `set_interface_designation` in 23; the top-20 crowders have a median description of 1,032 chars against 202 for tools that never crowd; missed tools average 407 chars against 728 for passing ones. Three defects in `score_tool`/`term_weights`, each a one-line shape: substring rather than whole-word matching, stopwords never zero-weighted, no length normalisation.

⭐ ABLATION, ONE FACTOR AT A TIME, on a Python replica that agrees with the live server on 164/180 ranks: whole-word alone does nothing (56→60); stopwords 56→45; length-norm 56→43; all three 56→39. **So scorer hygiene is real and bounded: about a third of the misses, not the story.** A fix that touched only the scorer would leave the twelve worst — the loop's own core reads and the most basic captures — exactly where they are.

🛑 REFUTED ON THE WAY: my first reading, that length bias was the dominant cause. It is a contributor. The decision's original framing — the register gap — is the larger half, and it was right before this was measured.

BOUNDS. Corpus author had read every description (not blind). One phrasing per tool. The Python replica splits on whitespace where Rust splits on non-alphanumerics; the 16 disagreeing ranks are punctuation. Whether option (b)'s phrasing would be filled honestly or just filled is the judgement-tier risk `fact:skill-mechanics-track-enforcement-exactly-and-they-split-into-three-kinds` names, and this corpus is what would measure it.
